Article Title: Oil price today: Brent crude jumps over 1% as traders await Hormuz reopening
Article Text:
Crude prices jump over 1% as Hormuz reopening

Oil prices rose over 1% on Monday as prospects of reopening Hormuz remained stuck in limbo. Brent crude gained 1.32% to $84.65 a barrel, around 7:30 am IST while WTI crude rose 1.04% to $78.99 a barrel.The rise came after both benchmarks fell more than 7% last week on expectations that Iran and Oman were close to reaching an agreement that could restore shipping through the strait. The waterway carried a fifth of the world's oil before the war.In the Middle East, Iran and Oman are close to a shipping-lane deal but Tehran is demanding more from Washington first. Earlier on Sunday, Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araqchi said that the agreement with Oman was in its "final stages". The pact would establish new shipping lanes through the Strait of Hormuz, but these would only be used once the US meets Tehran's conditions and the waterway is reopened, Iran's Mehr news agency quoted him as saying.Iran has said those conditions include compensation, an end to sanctions and an end to military threats from the US.The two nations, meanwhile, have not engaged in direct dialogue. Araqchi said that Tehran would not enter talks with Washington while the US was breaching an interim agreement signed in June.Messages between the two sides were instead being exchanged through intermediaries, he added.The uncertainty around Hormuz comes alongside attacks involving another key oil-producing country in the region.The Iran-aligned Houthi rebels said on Sunday that they had attacked Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery. Saudi Arabia's energy ministry confirmed that a fire had broken out at the refinery. It said the blaze had been extinguished, no injuries were reported and authorities were dealing with the incident, but did not provide a cause.The Houthis have also targeted shipping around the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, another oil chokepoint on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula. The attacks have taken place alongside Iranian strikes on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.Last month, the Yemeni rebel group announced a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia in the Red Sea, saying it was in response to what it described as a Saudi siege on the Houthis in Yemen. Riyadh has denied the allegation and supports Yemen's internationally recognised government.Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates' ADNOC said on Friday that 15 of its vessels had come under attack while passing through the Strait of Hormuz since the conflict began.The developments have kept uncertainty over the security of oil shipments through the region in focus as markets assess when the Strait of Hormuz could reopen. Though oil markets have remained volatile amid the ongoing geopolitical chaos, the spike is far lower than the $126 per barrel levels seen earlier during the war.
Article Summary: Brent crude gained 1.32% to $84.65 a barrel, while WTI crude rose 1.04% to £78.99 a barrel. Rise came after both benchmarks fell more than 7% last week on expectations that Iran and Oman were close to reaching an agreement that could restore shipping through the strait.

Article Title: Merchant charges for UPI soon? LS passes bill authorising govt to allow banks to levy fees - top facts
Article Text:
Government is likely to permit banks and payment service providers to levy a merchant discount rate of between 0.25% and 0.4% on UPI transactions exceeding Rs 2,000.

What the Bill means for UPI transactions

What RBI governor said on the bill

In a step closer to possibly introducing Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions, the Lok Sabha on Thursday approved a Bill amending the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.This empowers the government to allow banks and other payment service providers to impose charges on transactions conducted through the unified payments interface (UPI) and other electronic payment modes that may be notified.The amendment, cleared by the House without any discussion amid repeated disruptions, removes the existing legal restriction that bars banks and payment service providers from collecting MDR on notified electronic payment modes.According to a PTI report, through this move, the government intends to create a framework under which consumers and small businesses pay a nominal fee for digital payment services while ensuring banks, payment service providers (PSPs) and payment infrastructure companies that support the digital payments ecosystem have a sustainable source of revenue.The Bill seeks to delink the Payment and Settlement Systems Act from the Income Tax Act while providing the government with the legal authority to alter the existing zero-MDR framework governing UPI and RuPay card transactions.On Wednesday, The Times of India reported that the government is likely to permit banks and payment service providers to levy a merchant discount rate of between 0.25% and 0.4% on UPI transactions exceeding Rs 2,000 when payments are made to businesses, while person-to-person transfers are expected to remain exempt.According to official estimates, setting the threshold at Rs 2,000 would bring only about 5% of all UPI transactions within its scope. However, these transactions account for nearly 65% of the total value processed through the platform.As a result, routine purchases such as milk, vegetables, groceries, or payments for auto-rickshaw and taxi rides are unlikely to be affected. UPI recorded 23.7 billion transactions in July, with the total value estimated at Rs 29.9 lakh crore.The proposed change could pave the way for merchant charges to be introduced on certain UPI transactions, signalling a possible departure from India's current zero-charge digital payments model.Under the existing framework, banks and payment system providers are prohibited from imposing any direct or indirect charges on transactions carried out through UPI and RuPay debit cards.The proposed legislation empowers the central government to determine, through official notification, which electronic payment modes or categories of transactions will continue to remain exempt from such charges.Although the Bill does not itself impose a merchant discount rate or prescribe any fee, it establishes the legal foundation that would enable the government to revise the present zero-MDR framework at a later stage.The question of imposing MDR has remained a contentious issue, with banks and other participants in the payments industry consistently advocating its introduction, while the government has so far refrained from taking a decision even as digital payment platforms such as UPI have continued to witness robust growth.Some industry observers believe MDR could eventually be introduced for merchant-to-customer UPI transactions exceeding a specified value, while peer-to-peer transfers may continue to remain exempt.Unlike UPI transactions, which have so far remained free of such charges, real-time fund transfers carried out through RTGS and NEFT already attract a service fee."In the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, in Section 10A, for the words, figures and letters 'the electronic modes of payment prescribed under section 269SU of the Income-tax Act, 1961', the words 'one or more electronic modes of payment as the central government may, by notification, specify' shall be substituted with effect from the date of publication of this Act in the Official Gazette," the Bill said.Section 10A of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 bars banks and payment system providers from levying any fee on electronic payment transactions, while Section 269SU of the Income Tax Act mandates businesses with an annual turnover of more than Rs 50 crore to provide specified electronic payment options, including RuPay debit cards and BHIM-UPI QR codes.Commenting on the issue on Wednesday, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said it was "premature" to discuss the introduction of MDR on digital payment transactions.He stressed that continued investment in public infrastructure such as digital payments is essential and pointed out that the associated costs ultimately have to be borne by someone.Also Read | ‘Someone has to pay the cost’: RBI governor on MDR proposal for UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 "The choices before us are simple: either the general public has to pay for it through taxes, or we have to levy the merchant discount rate, following the 'user pays' model."Right now the government is getting us the amendment. Costs have to be paid by someone. We all want this public infrastructure to strengthen and become more efficient, etc. We continue to do that. That is our focus right now; let us wait and watch for further developments," Malhotra said.Malhotra reiterated that the key issue is that the cost of providing the service has to be borne by someone.He explained that under the 'user pays' model, MDR is charged to the merchant or the individual undertaking the transaction. However, he added that in the absence of MDR, the expense is effectively met by the public through tax revenues."What is important is that we continue to invest and continue to find the means, whether it is MDR or others. Let us wait and see how the situation evolves," he said.
Article Summary: Government is likely to permit banks and payment service providers to levy a merchant discount rate of between 0.25% and 0.4% on UPI transactions exceeding Rs 2,000. Person-to-person transfers are expected to remain exempt. UPI recorded 23.7 billion transactions in July.

Article Title: Will you have to pay to use UPI? FM Sitharaman clarifies who bears MDR
Article Text:
Union finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman speaking during the Monsoon session of Parliament

Panel to consider MDR after Bill is passed

FM links delay in debate to Parliament disruptions

Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Thursday pushed back Congress leader Jairam Ramesh's claims that ordinary people could end up paying more for using the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), clarifying that any Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on digital transactions would be levied on merchants and not on customers.Responding to Ramesh on social media platform X, Sitharaman said that the purpose of the MDR is to strengthen the digital payments ecosystem by enabling banks and fintech firms to invest in infrastructure, innovation and security."Before spreading a canard, @Jairam_Ramesh ji, please consider this: Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) applies only on the merchants and not on the end users/customers. It will support the Banks & Fintech to invest more on infrastructure, innovation & security. All users of UPI will reap the benefits of this investment."The finance minister also clarified that no decision has yet been taken on introducing an MDR on UPI transactions. She said the UPI and Services Steering Committee, headed by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), will examine the matter only after Parliament passes the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026.The proposed legislation empowers the central government to notify which electronic payment modes or transactions will continue to remain free.Sitharaman said the committee's deliberations on the merchant fee would take place only after the Bill receives parliamentary approval.The exchange followed a post by Jairam Ramesh, who argued that the burden of the Merchant Discount Rate would ultimately be borne by ordinary people. He also said the government's contention that such a charge is the only way to make UPI financially sustainable is "entirely wrong".Sitharaman rejected the assertion, maintaining that customers would not be required to pay the merchant fee.Sitharaman also criticised the opposition over repeated disruptions during the ongoing Monsoon session of Parliament, saying the proposed legislation could have been debated if proceedings had not been stalled.Referring to the disruptions in both the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha since the Monsoon session began on July 20, she said, "could have been discussed on the floor of the House if your party @INCIndia engages constructively in Parliament when the Bill was/is tabled. (LS/RS respectively)".The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026 proposes an amendment to Section 10(A) of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, giving the central government the legal authority to modify the existing zero-MDR framework for UPI and RuPay card transactions.The Bill itself does not introduce a Merchant Discount Rate or prescribe any fee. Instead, it creates the legal framework under which the government may decide to modify the current zero-MDR regime through a notification at a later stage.
Article Summary: Nirmala Sitharaman says any Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on digital transactions would be levied on merchants and not on customers. Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said ordinary people could end up paying more for using the Unified Payments Interface (UPI)

Article Title: Rupee slips to 95.28 against US dollar as oil, treasury yields remain elevated
Article Text:
Rupee slips to 95.28 against US dollar as oil, Treasury yields remain elevated

Rupee began Friday in red, falling 6 paise to 95.28 against the US dollar in early trade as a firmer greenback and higher US Treasury yields put pressure on the currency.The currency began the session at 95.27 at the interbank foreign exchange market before weakening to 95.28. This followed a 14-paise decline in the previous session, when the rupee ended at 95.22 against the dollar.Forex traders said dollar purchases by importers and profit-taking after the rupee's recent gains had outweighed the favourable global backdrop.The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against a basket of six major currencies, was trading 0.02 per cent higher at 99.95. Brent crude, meanwhile, gained 1.20 per cent to $83.48 a barrel in futures trade.Amit Pabari, MD of CR Forex Advisors, said that rupee could remain vulnerable, with oil prices, the dollar and US yields likely to influence its near-term movement."With oil back near $83, the dollar firm near 100, and US yields elevated, 95.00-95.10 stands out as a solid support for the rupee, and the currency climbing back towards the 96.00-96.20 zone looks like reality. Global developments, particularly around oil prices and the dollar, are likely to remain the key drivers for the rupee in the near term, keeping the overall bias tilted towards weakness," said CR Forex Advisors MD Amit Pabari.Anil Kumar Bhansali, head of treasury and executive director at Finrex Treasury Advisors LLP, said the dollar was also receiving support from higher US Treasury yields and renewed geopolitical concerns around the Strait of Hormuz."The rise in US Treasury yields and renewed geopolitical concerns around the Strait of Hormuz are providing some support to the dollar," said Anil Kumar Bhansali, Head of Treasury and Executive Director, Finrex Treasury Advisors LLP.Weakness in the currency came alongside a decline in domestic equities in early trade. Sensex was down 235.36 points at 78,699.80, while Nifty fell 24.30 points to 24,608.25.Foreign institutional investors were net sellers in the equity market on Thursday, offloading shares worth Rs 17.86 crore, according to exchange data.
Article Summary: Rupee slips to 95.28 against US dollar as oil, Treasury yields remain elevated. This followed a 14-paise decline in the previous session, when the rupee ended at 95.22. Brent crude, meanwhile, gained 1.20 per cent to $83.48 a barrel in futures trade.

Article Title: Maruti Suzuki chairman seeks faster reforms
Article Text:
In his message to shareholders in the company’s annual report for 2025-26, the veteran industry leader also requested all political parties to support reforms and programmes

NEW DELHI: Maruti Suzuki India chairman RC Bhargava has urged the Centre and state govts to proceed faster on the road of reforms and increase efforts to make doing business easier, while requesting all political parties to support reforms and programmes that create wealth.In his message to shareholders in the company’s annual report for 2025-26, the veteran industry leader also requested all political parties to support reforms and programmes that create wealth, and said the government and the opposition should “ensure that the additional resources that would be generated would be used to create a more equitable and just society”.
Article Summary: Maruti Suzuki India chairman RC Bhargava has urged the Centre and state govts to proceed faster on the road of reforms. In his message to shareholders in the company’s annual report for 2025-26, the veteran industry leader also requested all political parties to support reforms.

Article Title: Government mulls raising CCEA approval threshold for FDIs
Article Text:
CCEA is a high-level committee headed by PM Modi.

The government is considering a proposal to raise the threshold for foreign direct investment proposals requiring approval from the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) to Rs 15,000 crore from Rs 5,000 crore at present to further improve the country’s investment climate, according to sources. CCEA is a high-level committee headed by PM Modi. Its members include key Union Cabinet ministers such as the home minister and finance minister.
Article Summary: The government is considering a proposal to raise the threshold for foreign direct investment proposals requiring approval from the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs. CCEA is a high-level committee headed by PM Modi. Its members include key Union Cabinet ministers such as the home minister and finance minister.

Article Title: ‘Compliances major friction point for companies’
Article Text:
Citing an example, it said a typical firm operating in India currently navigates an archaic and disconnected web of regulations consisting of 1,536 distinct Acts, which collectively impose 69,233 separate compliance requirements and mandate 6,618 independent statutory filings across the three tiers of govt.

NEW DELHI: Stakeholders have informed a parliamentary committee that despite multi-phased central deregulation efforts, the absolute volume of business compliances remains a major friction point for domestic enterprises, according to the panel’s report.According to the department-related parliamentary standing committee on commerce’s report on ‘Doing Business in India: The Way Forward’, stakeholders apprised the panel that while pan-India rationalisation drives have successfully neutralised over 40,000 regulatory obligations, the survival of overlapping rules continues to inflate fixed operational costs and suppress long-term capital deployment.Citing an example, it said a typical firm operating in India currently navigates an archaic and disconnected web of regulations consisting of 1,536 distinct Acts, which collectively impose 69,233 separate compliance requirements and mandate 6,618 independent statutory filings across the three tiers of govt.The committee has noted that overlapping compliance requirements lead to duplication of effort.
Article Summary: Despite central deregulation efforts, the absolute volume of business compliances remains a major friction point for domestic enterprises. A typical firm operating in India currently navigates an archaic and disconnected web of regulations consisting of 1,536 distinct Acts. The committee has noted that overlapping compliance requirements lead to duplication of effort.

Article Title: Legally availabile marijuana in some countries adds to airline woes
Article Text:
Process of detecting consumption of psychoactive substances is difficult

NEW DELHI: The legal availability of marijuana for either medicinal or recreational use in places like Thailand and Amsterdam has made life difficult for airlines flying there. The reason: Unlike simple breath analyser tests for checking if the crew is tipsy, the process of detecting consumption of psychoactive substances is difficult. The only way to deter their consumption by flight crew members, say officials across multiple airlines, is to increase random dope testing as there substances usually remain present in the body for much longer than alcohol.The concern across airlines globally to check this stems from the fact that operating a flight “under the influence of any psychoactive substance might render (licensed personnel like pilots) unable to safely and properly exercise” perform their duty, according to International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO).Possibly the most infamous case of this was a US carrier’s off duty pilot travelling on the jump seat (extra seat behind pilots operating the flight) in the flight deck trying to shut down the engines. This off duty pilot had reportedly taken psychedelic mushrooms two days before the incident and hadn't slept in 48 hours.“This is a challenge globally. Often the tests are not conclusive if taking some medicine leads to detection of psychoactive substances.However, recent consumption of drugs does show up in tests,” said senior officials.The DGCA rules on “procedure for examination of the aviation personnel for consumption of psychoactive substances” says: “In case the confirmatory test is found positive, the medical in charge of the concerned organisation shall consult a medical review officer (MRO) to determine if the result was due to a legitimate therapeutic treatment or some other innocuous source (for example pain relief medication containing codeine may trigger a positive result for opiates). ”Airlines abroad and in India try to create awareness and encourage employees to anonymously report addiction so that the same can be addressed. But mostly people avoid reporting the same, so this virtually remains a non-starter, said many officials. Officials running operations across airlines say the focus in India is primarily on self-reporting and de-addiction.“But given the easy availability of psychoactive substances, we need to make the consequences a bit tougher and act as deterrent. We have to increase random testing, that’s the only way out,” said officials. Under current DGCA rules, all scheduled airlines commercial and air navigation service provider need to test at least 10% of their flight crew members and air traffic controllers every year.
Article Summary: The legal availability of marijuana for either medicinal or recreational use in places like Thailand and Amsterdam has made life difficult for airlines flying there. Unlike simple breath analyser tests for checking if the crew is tipsy, the process of detecting consumption of psychoactive substances is difficult. The only way to deter their consumption is to increase random dope testing.

Article Title: Spooked by CAS, retail traders call for boycott
Article Text:
“One day trading boycott against regulations and rising taxes impacting retail traders,” said another post with over 15,000 followers.

MUMBAI: Day traders have started an online campaign to boycott trading for a day in the stock market on Aug 12, in protest against the recently introduced Closing Auction Session (CAS). They feel the new system is working against them and in favour of large institutions. The protest is also against ‘frequent rule changes’ by the regulator, and ‘high taxes’, several social media posts said.“No trade day on Aug 12. Against STT (securities transaction tax). Against CAS,” said a trader on X (formerly Twitter) with nearly 1.5 lakh followers. “One day trading boycott against regulations and rising taxes impacting retail traders,” said another post with over 15,000 followers.The recently introduced CAS, a mechanism to determine the closing price of about 200 stocks that are also traded in the derivatives segments of the bourses, has led to wide divergence between the two leading indices, Nifty and sensex. Closing prices of some of these stocks have also shown divergence. Traders have alleged that due to this they have suffered substantial losses.
Article Summary: Day traders have started an online campaign to boycott trading for a day in the stock market on Aug 12. They feel the new system is working against them and in favour of large institutions. The protest is also against ‘frequent rule changes’ by the regulator, and ‘high taxes’

Article Title: CERT-In: Cyber threats for fin, healthcare stay elevated
Article Text:
The healthcare sector recorded another 18,855 instances in the first six months, equivalent to nearly 55% of the 34,480 detected and mitigated during all of 2025.

NEW DELHI: Cyber threat activity targeting India’s finance and healthcare sectors remained elevated in the first half of 2026, with detections already crossing 60% of the levels recorded during the whole of last year, according to data shared by govt in Parliament.CERT-In detected and mitigated almost 3.5 lakh instances of malicious scanning, probing and vulnerable services in the finance sector between Jan and June. This compares with 5.7 lakh instances during the whole of 2025.The healthcare sector recorded another 18,855 instances in the first six months, equivalent to nearly 55% of the 34,480 detected and mitigated during all of 2025. Together, finance and healthcare accounted for just under 3.7 lakh instances in the first half. However, targeted intrusion campaigns against banks did not show a similar increase. CERT-In detected and mitigated 17 such campaigns during Jan-June 2026, compared with 39 during the whole of 2025.The data also pointed to wider cybersecurity preparedness exercises for critical infrastructure. CERT-In conducted two exercises for the power sector in H1 2026, involving 274 participants from 103 organisations, including utilities, system operators and generation, transmission and distribution entities.Significantly, one of the exercises focused on countering emerging cybersecurity risks posed by frontier AI models, indicating that threats linked to advanced AI systems are now being incorporated into preparedness drills for critical infrastructure. In comparison, CERT-In conducted three power-sector cybersecurity exercises during 2025, involving 150 participants from 30 organisations.
Article Summary: CERT-In detected and mitigated almost 3.5 lakh instances of malicious scanning, probing and vulnerable services in the finance sector between Jan and June. This compares with 5.7 lakh instances during the whole of 2025. The healthcare sector recorded another 18,855 instances in the first six months.

Article Title: Foreign funds invest 12.9k cr in Aug 1st week
Article Text:
FPIs had withdrawn Rs 49,340 crore in June, Rs 32,963 crore in May, Rs 60,847 crore in April and a massive Rs 1.2 lakh crore in March. Prior to this selling streak, they had invested Rs 22,615 crore in Feb, according to CDSL data.

NEW DELHI: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) sustained their buying momentum in Indian equities, investing Rs 12,921 crore in the first week of Aug, driven by improving macroeconomic conditions, expectations of US rate cuts, lower crude oil prices and a stable rupee. The inflow follows a Rs 20,200-crore investment in July, marking a sharp turnaround after four consecutive months of heavy selling.FPIs had withdrawn Rs 49,340 crore in June, Rs 32,963 crore in May, Rs 60,847 crore in April and a massive Rs 1.2 lakh crore in March. Prior to this selling streak, they had invested Rs 22,615 crore in Feb, according to CDSL data.Despite the recent buying spree, foreign investors have remained net sellers in Indian equities in 2026, withdrawing Rs 2.4 lakh crore so far, already exceeding the Rs 1.7 lakh crore outflow recorded during the entire 2025.Market experts said the recent inflows reflect improving investor sentiment, supported by expectations of US rate cuts, softer crude oil prices and a stable rupee.The RBI’s improved growth and inflation outlook has further strengthened confidence, while relatively low foreign ownership of Indian equities leaves room for fresh allocations, said Vedant Gupte, co-founder and CEO of investment platform Trackk.Importantly, a large share of the recent buying has come through the secondary market, signalling stronger interest in listed Indian companies rather than merely IPO allocations, Gupte added.
Article Summary: FPIs had withdrawn Rs 49,340 crore in June, Rs 32,963 crore in May, Rs 60,847 crore in April and a massive Rs 1.2 lakh crore in March. Prior to this selling streak, they had invested Rs 22,615 crore in Feb, according to CDSL data.

Article Title: LIC chief flags pressure of global turmoil on industry
Article Text:
On premium basis, the persistency was 75.3% and 61.1%, respectively and 75.6% and 63.9%, for the comparable period last year.

MUMBAI: Economic and geopolitical uncertainty is beginning to weigh on household savings and insurance demand, with LIC reporting pressure on long-term policy persistency and caution in premium growth even as its first-quarter profit and value of new business rose quite sharply.On Thursday, after announcement of the company’s results, LIC MD & CEO R Doraiswamy said uncertainty in the macro environment could affect policyholders’ ability to pay renewal premiums on time.For Q1FY27, the persistency ratios on number of policies basis for the 13th month and 61st month were 66.5% and 48.7%, respectively. The comparable persistency ratios for the corresponding period ended June 30th, 2025 were 64.4% and 51.1%, respectively.On premium basis, the persistency was 75.3% and 61.1%, respectively and 75.6% and 63.9%, for the comparable period last year. This indicates that the lapsation was among the low value policies.“When macro environments present uncertainty, short-term pressure can affect policyholders’ ability to pay renewal premiums on time,” Doraiswamy said.He attributed the decline in long-term persistency to seasonal economic factors and tighter household savings, adding that LIC was following up with customers to revive policies.The caution is also visible in the flow of new business. LIC’s total premium income rose 6.8% to Rs 1,27,250 crore in the first quarter, while annualised premium equivalent stood at Rs 13,692 crore. Doraiswamy said premium and APE growth reflected a “somewhat cautious environment” despite the company’s strong quarterly performance.
Article Summary: LIC’s total premium income rose 6.8% to Rs 1,27,250 crore in the first quarter. Annualised premium equivalent stood at Rs 13,692 crore. “When macro environments present uncertainty, short-term pressure can affect policyholders’ ability to pay renewal premiums on time,” says CEO.

Article Title: No going back on strategic sale of PSUs, ministries told
Article Text:
Officials acknowledged that several govt departments had started turning inter-ministerial meetings into a forum for seeking a review, with some of them repeatedly approaching Niti Aayog and other agencies suggesting a review.

TOI

NEW DELHI: The Centre has ruled out diluting the list of public sector enterprises lined up for strategic sale amid repeated demands from heavy industries, fertiliser and housing ministries for a review.Over the last few months, govt has engaged in an extensive exercise reviewing the list of public sector companies that have been identified for privatisation, listing and closure, with the PM’s Office involved in the process. While individual ministries have managed to get several of the PSUs that were originally on the sell-off list — such as BPCL and Shipping Corp — out of the govt’s scheme, multiple officials toldthat there is little possibility of further dilution.Officials acknowledged that several govt departments had started turning inter-ministerial meetings into a forum for seeking a review, with some of them repeatedly approaching Niti Aayog and other agencies suggesting a review.The message from top is, however, clear that all ministries have to work together in achieving the goal of strategic sale, especially at a time when govt is keen to maximise revenue and also send a message that it is serious about the exercise.Despite govt’s commitment to disinvestment, over the years, the process had become haphazard with no centralised list even in place. Over the years, the companies that were being pursued for privatisation were also lost on the way, be it BEML or Shipping Corp.Even now, just one entity — IDBI Bank — is sought to be privatised with all eyes on the Prem Vatsa-owned Fairfax and Emirates NBD being the two bidders in the fray. While both have investments in Indian banks, Catholic Syrian Bank and RBL, respectively, they are keen on being part of the exercise. For either, RBI will have to step in and provide some exemption to facilitate running two banking entities in the country.Officials indicated that given the current emphasis on offer-for-sale and initial public offers, strategic sale cases will be identified once the IDBI Bank deal closes.With govt in the third year of its current term, it will have to move quickly so that more transactions can be pursued. The Centre has already raised upwards of Rs 60,000 crore from disinvestment and with IDBI Bank sale, if it materialises this time, and other small stake sales lined up, it is on course to beat the Rs 80,000 crore target.
Article Summary: The Centre has ruled out diluting the list of public sector enterprises lined up for strategic sale amid repeated demands from heavy industries, fertiliser and housing ministries for a review. Over the years, the process had become haphazard with no centralised list even in place. Even now, just one entity — IDBI Bank — is sought to be privatised.

Article Title: As demand shoots up, banks strengthen gold loan muscle
Article Text:
Indian Bank has identified 725 branches as Gold Shoppe branches with dedicated staff and enhanced customer service facilities. The bank has added 982 empanelled appraisers in the past six months, taking the total to 3,538.

CHENNAI/MUMBAI: Banks are strengthening branch-level gold loan capabilities by adding appraisers, investing in testing equipment and digitising processing as demand surges and lenders challenge NBFCs that dominate the market.NBFCs built scale through fast 30-minute disbursals backed by in-house jewellers and X-ray fluorescence testing. Now, banks are copying this model by expanding branch-level appraisal teams and digitising processing to cut turnaround time. Union Bank of India, whose gold loan portfolio is growing about 30% annually, deploys dedicated jewellers at branches handling more than a dozen proposals a day. These appraisers use weighing equipment, touchstones and acid testing kits to assess jewellery. Branches with lower volumes share appraisers across locations. The bank said customers at its 1,671 gold loan points typically receive loans within 30 minutes. Indian Bank has identified 725 branches as Gold Shoppe branches with dedicated staff and enhanced customer service facilities. The bank has added 982 empanelled appraisers in the past six months, taking the total to 3,538.For banks, gold loans, the fastest-growing segment, have expanded 105% year-on-year in May to about Rs 5.2 lakh crore according to RBI data.However, banks report lower growth of around 30% because they classify gold loans across agriculture, personal and MSME loan categories. Credit bureau CRIF estimates the gold loan market at Rs 18.6 lakh crore at end-March 2026, up 50.4%, with NBFCs still dominant despite banks gaining share.An Indian Bank official said the lender has reduced approval time to around 15 minutes through system-driven due diligence, automated validations, digital appraisal, technology-enabled credit processing, automated loan disbursement and automated settlement of appraiser fees.The bank has also developed a mobile application for empanelled appraisers that captures appraisal details and ornament particulars digitally and integrates them with the loan processing system. Digital documentation through NESL e-sign platform has further reduced manual intervention and shortened processing time.Indian Overseas Bank has expanded its panel to 2,910 empanelled gold appraisers and introduced digital valuation controls, digital communication of loan documents and workflow-based monitoring. The system tracks every stage of processing, identifies pending actions and generates management reports for monitoring. “We have expanded the panel of qualified gold appraisers, and upgraded gold loan processing platform. In normal cases, where all documents are in order, the bank completes the gold loan process within approximately 15 minutes, enabling customers to receive timely financial assistance,” IOB MD and CEO Ajay Kumar Srivastava said.Federal Bank, which has a gold loan portfolio of about Rs 40,000 crore, has built in-house appraisal capability across its network. “We are the largest bank in gold loans and we have achieved this by building the appraisal capability,” said KVS Manian, MD and CEO.
Article Summary: NBFCs built scale through fast 30-minute disbursals backed by in-house jewellers and X-ray fluorescence testing. Banks are copying this model by expanding branch-level appraisal teams and digitising processing. Indian Bank has identified 725 branches as Gold Shoppe branches with dedicated staff and enhanced customer service facilities.

Article Title: Clean power push: India hits 300 GW non-fossil capacity milestone ahead of 2030 target
Article Text:
India crossed 300 GW of non-fossil fuel-based installed power generation capacity as of July 31 (representative image)

Solar accounts for more than half of non-fossil capacity

Renewable power generation more than doubles

India has 200 GW to add by 2030

India has crossed 300 GW of installed non-fossil fuel-based electricity generation capacity, reaching more than 60 per cent of its target of 500 GW by 2030, according to the ministry of new and renewable energy.As of July 31, the country's total non-fossil fuel capacity stood at 300.50 GW, while overall installed electricity generation capacity was around 552 GW.This means non-fossil sources now account for more than 54 per cent of India's total installed power capacity, the ministry said in a statement.Solar power remains the largest component of India's non-fossil capacity at 164.59 GW, followed by wind power at 58.14 GW and hydro power at 57.24 GW.The remaining capacity comprises 11.75 GW of bio-power and 8.78 GW of nuclear power.Solar capacity has increased sharply from 2.8 GW in 2014 to around 165 GW currently.Wind power capacity has also risen from 21 GW in 2014 to 58.14 GW.The government said India added a record 55.29 GW of non-fossil fuel-based electricity capacity in 2025-26.Solar accounted for 44.6 GW of the additions, while wind contributed 6 GW.The increase in installed capacity has also been accompanied by higher renewable electricity generation.According to the ministry, renewable energy generation increased from 190.96 billion units (BU) in 2014-15 to 477.79 BU in 2025-26.Domestic manufacturing capacity for solar equipment has also expanded. The capacity listed under the Approved List of Models and Manufacturers (ALMM) for solar photovoltaic modules has crossed 200 GW, compared with 2.3 GW in 2014.The ministry attributed the expansion to measures including the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme, which supports domestic manufacturing of high-efficiency solar modules.With non-fossil capacity at 300.50 GW as of July 31, India needs to add roughly 199.5 GW to reach its stated target of 500 GW by 2030.The ministry said the expansion is also being accompanied by efforts to reduce industrial emissions and develop the green hydrogen sector.It is implementing the National Green Hydrogen Mission, with the stated aim of developing India as a hub for the production, use and export of green hydrogen and its derivatives.The latest capacity figures were released by the ministry of new and renewable energy.
Article Summary: As of July 31, the country's total non-fossil fuel capacity stood at 300.50 GW. Solar power remains the largest component at 164.59 GW, followed by wind power at 58.14 GW and hydro power at 57.24 GW. The remaining capacity comprises 11.75 GW of bio-power and 8.78 GW of nuclear power.

Article Title: Thailand school shooting: Student opens fire; 7 dead
Article Text:
Teacher and gunman dead, four injured in Thailand school shooting

This is a developing story

At least seven people, including a teacher, were killed and 15 others injured after a student opened fire at a school north of Bangkok on Friday.Police said the suspected gunman was also killed in the incident.Lt Col Pasakorn Chaitawiwong, head of the Plai Bang subdistrict police department, told Reuters that the number of fatalities was still being ascertained.The shooting took place in the Bang Kruai district, with police identifying the suspected perpetrator as a student. Authorities have not provided further details about the incident.
Article Summary: At least seven people, including a teacher, were killed and 15 others injured after a student opened fire at a school north of Bangkok. Article Title: Rahul Gandhi reveals his favourite BJP leader in candid Gen Z 'Ask Me Anything' on Instagram
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi launched an Instagram "Ask Me Anything" session for young people





NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Thursday launched an "Ask Me Anything" session on Instagram as part of a fresh outreach to Gen Z, responding to questions on student protests, women's education, politics and even lighter topics such as Batman.Sharing the initiative on X, the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha wrote, "Students, Gen-Z -- I'm here to listen. Ask me anything on Instagram, and I'll answer as many questions as I can." The Congress later shared video clips of his responses.Responding to a question on the ongoing student agitation in Jharkhand over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, Gandhi said the country's education system had "collapsed" and urged governments across party lines to pay attention to students' concerns."The student protests that are happening in the country are against the education system. I have said it in Kota, Dehradun and will say it in Allahabad that our education system has collapsed. It is unaffordable and oppressive," Gandhi said."Every government, whether it is the Centre, a Congress government or the Jharkhand government, should listen to what students are saying and take action to change the education system," he added.The protest in Jharkhand entered its 13th day on Thursday, with six demonstrators continuing an indefinite hunger strike. Student groups have formed an 11-member delegation for talks with the state government over their demands.Asked what message he had for young women fighting for their right to education, Gandhi said women deserved equal — if not greater — space in every sphere of life."India's women are our biggest strength. I do not appreciate the way women are treated in society, in our education system or in the corporate sector. You be confident, you be brave, you be powerful exactly as you are, and we are there to fully support you," he said.In one of the lighter moments of the interaction, Gandhi was asked to name his favourite politician from the BJP. He named former Punjab chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh, saying they got along well and praising his knowledge of military history.On the state of education, Gandhi alleged that the system was "busy destroying thinkers" and claimed that after being "captured" by the RSS, its focus had shifted to discouraging independent thinking among young people.Asked if he was Batman, Gandhi joked, "Let's just say that no one has ever seen me and Batman in the same room together."Replying to a question on the philosophy that inspires him the most, Gandhi referred to the ideas of Lord Buddha, Guru Nanak Dev, Basavanna, Sankardev, Birsa Munda, Periyar, Mahatma Phule, Narayana Guru, B R Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi, among others, saying these traditions had shaped India's Constitution.The Instagram interaction came a day after Gandhi met students who had protested over the NEET paper leak and allegedly faced police action last month. On Wednesday, he accused Union home minister Amit Shah of being responsible for the violence against the protesters and claimed the government had failed to explain the incident in Parliament.Gandhi has increasingly been using Instagram to engage with students and young voters. The platform has emerged as a key battleground for political outreach, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union ministers and leaders across parties also stepping up their engagement with Gen Z audiences.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi launched an "Ask Me Anything" session on Instagram. He responded to questions on student protests, women's education, politics and even lighter topics. Gandhi has increasingly been using Instagram to engage with students and young voters. The platform has emerged as a key battleground for political outreach.

Article Title: 'We are children, not terrorists': Students on hunger strike urge Jharkhand CM to meet protesters
Article Text:
Student Rahul Kranti, who has been on hunger strike, said his health condition had deteriorated due to prolonged fasting.





RANCHI: The protest over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations in Jharkhand entered its 14th day on Friday, with six students continuing their hunger strike. Meanwhile, two student organisations announced plans to march towards the state Assembly, which is currently in session.The development comes amid a deadlock between the protesting aspirants and the state government, with students claiming that they have not received any formal invitation for talks to address their concerns.Student Rahul Kranti, who has been on hunger strike, said his health condition had deteriorated due to prolonged fasting.He claimed he was suffering from severe weakness and headaches and alleged that medicines prescribed by a medical team had not been provided despite assurances."A team of doctors visited yesterday evening and I informed them about my condition. They prescribed medicines, but the government medical team did not provide them. They said they would arrange them within two to three hours, but an entire night has passed and we are still waiting," Kranti told PTI.Protesters seek direct meeting with CM Hemant Soren Kranti said the protesting students were not interested in closed-door discussions and wanted chief minister Hemant Soren to meet them directly at the protest site."We do not want discussions behind closed doors. We want the Chief Minister to come to us. We are his children and the people of the state," he said.The student leader urged Soren to publicly address their demands and announce an investigation into examinations conducted during his government's first and second terms."Our demands publicly, and announce that all examinations conducted during the Hemant Soren government's first and second terms will be investigated by the Central Bureau of Investigation. That is our only demand. He only needs to come for five minutes and speak to us," Kranti added.Rejecting any suggestion of violence or misconduct, Kranti said the movement had remained peaceful since its beginning."We are his children and the people of the state. Does he consider us terrorists that he cannot come among us? We have conducted our protest peacefully, and there has not been a single complaint that we have resorted to violence or made any bad statements," he added.The agitation has increased political pressure on the Hemant Soren-led government, with opposition parties raising questions over alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations and demanding accountability.The demonstrators have been demanding the cancellation of the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) Civil Services Examination and an independent investigation into the alleged irregularities in the recruitment process. They have sought a probe either by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) or by a committee of retired High Court judges from outside the state.The protesters have also called for comprehensive reforms in the functioning of the Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) to ensure transparency in future recruitment examinations.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Student Rahul Kranti, who has been on hunger strike, said his health condition had deteriorated due to prolonged fasting. Two student organisations announced plans to march towards the state Assembly, which is currently in session. The development comes amid a deadlock between the protesting aspirants and the state government.

Article Title: Gurgaon rain chaos: Offices shift to work from home as flooded roads cripple traffic
Article Text:
Heavy rain cripples Gurgaon, work from home advisory issued for offices.

Torrential rain has caused significant flooding and infrastructure failures across Gurgaon.





GURGAON: Torrential rain and another collapse of civic infrastructure forced Gurgaon - the state's corporate capital - into an unplanned work-from-home mode on Thursday after flooded stretches, submerged underpasses and hours long traffic snarls prompted police and the district administration to ask companies to keep employees off roads.The advisory effectively turned the remainder of the workweek into a long weekend for thousands of corporate employees, who are now expected to return to offices only on Monday - weather and the city's infrastructure permitting.The decision came after another chaotic morning that saw the Medanta and IFFCO Chowk underpasses shut because of flooding, a portion of the road near The Westin cave in and arterial stretches remain choked for hours. The city recorded 97mm of rain between 8am on Wednesday and 8am on Thursday. While IMD issued an orange alert for Gurgaon, neighbouring Delhi was placed under a red alert as heavy rain battered NCR.It was city police who first appealed to companies on social media to allow employees to work remotely to reduce congestion. Hours later, district disaster management authority (DDMA) issued a formal advisory asking all corporate offices and private institutions to permit work from home "wherever feasible" on Thursday and Friday.Officials said limiting vehicular movement would ease gridlock and allow civic agencies to repair damaged roads, clear drains and tackle widespread waterlogging. But the advisory also underscored how repeated failures of civic infrastructure after a spell of rain had begun affecting not just traffic but also business continuity in one of the country's largest corporate hubs.For much of corporate Gurgaon, the decision effectively ended the working week early. With Friday covered under WFH and Saturday and Sunday being weekly offs for most offices, thousands of employees will now work remotely until the weekend ends.Most technology, consulting and financial services firms shifted seamlessly to remote operations, but the disruption extended well beyond office attendance. Client meetings were cancelled or moved online, training sessions deferred and vendor interactions rescheduled. Businesses dependent on office crowds - such as roadside eateries, restaurants, taxis, transport operators and retailers in commercial districts - also witnessed a sharp drop in footfall.The impact was more pronounced in industrial belts such as Manesar and Udyog Vihar, where manufacturing continued but employee movement, logistics and supply chains were hit by flooded roads and traffic snarls. Several companies staggered shifts, delayed reporting times and arranged transport for essential staff."This isn't just about employees working from home. Gurgaon's economy runs on the daily movement of lakhs of professionals. When that movement stops, everyone - from office cafeterias and taxis to hotels and retailers - feels the impact," an industry representative said.The city's most visible reminder of its recurring monsoon woes was the Medanta underpass, which was once again submerged under knee-deep water after overnight rain, forcing authorities to shut one of the busiest links and divert traffic via the Rajiv Chowk U-turn. The underpass remained closed till Thursday evening as operations continued to pump out water. Earlier this week, the Ambience Mall and Bajghera underpasses were also shut after heavy rain left commuters stranded and triggered massive traffic jams.NHAI officials said the Medanta underpass was flooded because it is connected to a GMDA master stormwater drain that itself overflowed during the downpour. "The pumps installed at the underpass discharge into the same drain. Once the drain overflowed, the water started backflowing into the underpass despite the pumps being operational," an official said, adding that two additional high-capacity pumps had been deployed to speed up dewatering.The IFFCO Chowk underpass was also shut for nearly two hours after water entered the carriageway, while continuous rain led to a road cave-in near The Westin. The damaged stretch was barricaded and traffic diverted while repairs were planned. DCP (traffic) Prateek Gaholot said other waterlogged underpasses were closed as a precaution to prevent accidents.Commuters said the WFH advisory came only after they had spent hours battling flooded roads and slow traffic."I left home around 8am, but spent nearly two hours covering what usually takes 30 minutes. My manager eventually asked the entire team to return home and log in remotely because reaching office had become impossible," said Rohit Sharma, an IT professional at Cyber Hub.Vijay Shiv Nath, a resident of Malibu Towne, said flooding at the Medanta underpass had become an annual ordeal. "Almost every time it rains heavily, the underpass is closed. I use it to avoid Rajiv Chowk, but once it shuts, the diversion itself becomes chaotic. A 30-minute journey stretched to nearly an hour on Thursday," he added.Neha Arora, who works with a multinational consulting firm in Udyog Vihar, said teams facing clients had to quickly redraw their schedules. "We cancelled in-person meetings, postponed presentations and shifted everything online. Several colleagues were stranded in traffic, while others were dealing with power and internet disruptions at home," she added.The disruption was mirrored across Delhi too, where heavy rain during the morning rush hour left roads waterlogged and traffic crawling on NH-8, Delhi-Meerut Expressway, the Safdarjung-AIIMS corridor, Hauz Khas, Aruna Asaf Ali Marg, Ber Sarai and Munirka.
Article Summary: Torrential rain has caused significant flooding and infrastructure failures across Gurgaon. Police and the district administration asked companies to keep employees off roads. The decision came after another chaotic morning that saw the Medanta and IFFCO Chowk underpasses shut because of flooding.

Article Title: Berkshire Hathaway Q2 earnings: Profit rises 16% to $12.98 billion as buybacks accelerate
Article Text:
Greg Abel's second quarter as CEO

American multinational conglomerate Berkshire Hathaway reported stronger-than-expected second-quarter results, with operating profit, revenue and net income rising, while its massive cash pile fell as the company stepped up stock purchases and buybacks.Operating profit rose 16 per cent year-on-year to $12.98 billion, beating analyst expectations, reported Reuters. Revenue increased 10 per cent to $101.81 billion, while net income more than doubled to $25.67 billion. The net income figure includes unrealised gains and losses on Berkshire's investments.The improvement came despite weaker results from Geico, Berkshire's auto insurance business. Higher profits at BNSF Railway and businesses including NetJets and TTI helped offset the insurer's decline.Berkshire also repurchased $4.5 billion of its own shares between April and June and bought another $3.3 billion worth in July, accelerating a buyback programme that had resumed in March after a nearly two-year pause.The company also bought nearly $20 billion more stocks than it sold during the quarter, ending 14 consecutive quarters as a net seller.One of its biggest purchases was an additional $10 billion investment in Alphabet, the parent company of Google and YouTube.Berkshire ended June with $364.7 billion in cash and cash equivalents, down from a record $380.2 billion three months earlier. The figure also reflects the $6.8 billion Berkshire spent in July to acquire homebuilder Taylor Morrison.The pace of buybacks marks a significant change from the period when Warren Buffett struggled to find attractive opportunities for Berkshire's cash. The company repurchased a record $27 billion of its own shares in 2021.Meanwhile, Geico's pre-tax underwriting profit fell 45 per cent as accident claims increased and the company spent more on advertising to attract customers.Overall profit from Berkshire's insurance and reinsurance businesses fell 11%.Analyst Cathy Seifert described Geico's results as "absolutely abysmal" and said they raised concerns about the insurer's performance compared with rivals such as Allstate and Progressive.On the other hand, BNSF Railway's profit rose 6 per cent to $1.56 billion as the railroad transported more consumer, agricultural and energy products and benefited from higher fuel charges.Berkshire Hathaway Energy reported a 27 per cent increase in profit to $891 million, helped by stronger utility margins and tax credits.The results mark the second quarter since Greg Abel succeeded Warren Buffett as Berkshire's chief executive.Investors have been watching how Abel approaches Berkshire's enormous capital reserves and investment decisions after Buffett's long tenure.Berkshire's policy allows it to buy back shares when management believes they are trading below their intrinsic value. Abel determines that value conservatively after consulting Buffett, who remains the company's chairman.Despite the stronger quarterly results, Berkshire's Class A shares have underperformed the S&P 500 since Abel's succession was announced in May 2025. The shares have gained 3% in 2026, compared with a 13% rise in the S&P 500.Berkshire also warned that considerable uncertainty remains around the broader economic and geopolitical environment, including tariffs and wars, with consumer businesses such as Fruit of the Loom and Forest River reflecting changes in consumer confidence.
Article Summary: Operating profit rose 16 per cent year-on-year to $12.98 billion. Revenue increased 10 per cent to $101.81 billion, while net income more than doubled to $25.67 billion. Higher profits at BNSF Railway and businesses including NetJets and TTI helped offset the insurer's decline.

Article Title: From H-1B to H-1Bye-bye: Trump targets 60-day grace period for laid off foreign workers
Article Text:
US may scrap H-1B’s 60-day job-loss cushion, putting Indian workers on an immigration clock

TOI correspondent from Washington:

For highly skilled foreign workers in America, a majority of whom are from India, the Trump administration has apparently decided that losing a job isn't stressful enough. Why not add an immigration cliff?The department of homeland security is advancing a proposal to eliminate the 60-day grace period that allows H-1B workers and certain other legal nonimmigrants to remain in the US after their employment ends while they find another sponsor, change status, or prepare to leave.The proposed rule, RIN 1615-AD22, went to the White House office of information and regulatory affairs for review Thursday. It is not yet law. Under current regulations, an H-1B worker whose employment ends can generally remain in the US for up to 60 days -- or until the authorized stay expires, whichever comes first. The grace period was created by a DHS regulation that took effect in 2017, recognizing a rather obvious fact about modern employment: companies sometimes fire people.Without it, the immigration consequences of a Friday layoff could begin with remarkable speed. An H-1B worker could fall out of status when qualifying employment ends and would have to quickly find another lawful immigration solution or prepare to leave. A new employer could file a petition, but the worker could no longer count on a two-month cushion to make that happen.That is an especially formidable deadline for someone who must not merely find a job, but find an employer willing and able to sponsor an H-1B, complete the paperwork and get the immigration process moving.For an American worker, eight weeks can disappear between interviews, negotiations, background checks and the inevitable corporate email saying, “We're moving in a different direction.”For an H-1B professional from India or elsewhere, those same eight weeks are an immigration lifeline. And these workers are not necessarily recent arrivals with a suitcase beside the front door. Many have lived in America for years, bought homes, obtained mortgages, paid taxes, put children through American schools and built careers and communities. A layoff can threaten not merely a paycheck but an entire household's established life.There is another, less obvious consequence: employer leverage. The existing grace period gives an H-1B worker breathing room to negotiate a move to another company. Remove it, and workers may become reluctant to tell their employers they are leaving until a new H-1B filing is safely underway. That could give existing employers less notice and make job transitions less orderly.The proposal is being welcomed by immigration restrictionist allies such as US tech workers, which campaigns against what it considers excessive use of foreign labor by corporate America. It argues that H-1B is a temporary program and questions why a worker should remain after the job that justified the visa disappears. The argument is straightforward: temporary worker, temporary job, temporary stay. The counterargument is equally straightforward: people are not disposable light bulbs.The proposal fits a broader Trump approach that has made legal immigration itself more precarious through higher fees, intensified scrutiny, tighter visa policies, and measures that increase the dependence of temporary foreign workers on their sponsoring employers.While all that may please immigration restrictionists, it creates an awkward contradiction for corporate America. The US admits H-1B workers because employers say they need specialized talent, yet the administration would make those same workers less secure when an employer decides it no longer needs them.America has long benefited from attracting engineers, scientists, physicians, entrepreneurs and technology specialists from around the world. The implicit bargain was simple: come here, work hard, pay taxes and build a life. The emerging bargain increasingly sounds different: come here, work hard, pay taxes — and remember that your entire American existence may depend on your employer's quarterly earnings report.The irony is that the 60-day grace period was hardly an immigration giveaway. It does not authorize indefinite residence or employment; it simply gives workers a limited window to find another lawful status, obtain a new sponsor or organize their departure. DHS itself has acknowledged the vulnerability created when workers unexpectedly lose employment. In a 2024 rulemaking concerning H-2 workers, it said grace periods can give workers time to respond to sudden employment changes, seek new employment or organize their departure.The proposed H-1B rollback therefore represents more than the disappearance of 60 calendar days. It would tell highly skilled foreign professionals contemplating America that their jobs may be temporary; increasingly, so may be their place in the country.For an administration determined to make America harder to enter and harder to remain in, that may be precisely the point. For an economy competing globally for talent, however, it could prove an unusually expensive way of saying: “Please don't get too comfortable.”
Article Summary: US may scrap H-1B’s 60-day job-loss cushion, putting Indian workers on an immigration clock. For an American worker, eight weeks can disappear between interviews, negotiations, background checks and the inevitable corporate email saying, “We're moving in a different direction”

Article Title: US employers cut 23k jobs amid war strain

The unemployment rate dipped to 4.1% only because Americans left the job market

US employers unexpectedly cut 23,000 jobs last month, and labour department revisions shaved 1,03,000 jobs off payrolls in May and June.
